prompt.context: American Beauty Company (ABC) is a high-quality beauty products company. They have performed well both in the US and globally and enjoy strong brand recognition. One of their major products is hair color. ABC manufactures high-quality 'use at home' hair color products, sold through retail and drugstores, with all manufacturing in-house. They also operate an 800 number for customer support. Recently they have been experiencing declining revenues and market share. Retailers have complained about their products as competition from Bell International increases. The firm has been called in to advise ABC on what to do.
prompt.question: How would you start thinking about this problem?

clarifying_info.q: What segments does ABC compete in?
clarifying_info.a: Their biggest market segment is 18-55 year old women, but they also serve men and teens.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current market size and growth rate by segment?
clarifying_info.a: Women: $800M, 5% growth; Men: $200M, 20% growth; Teens: $100M, 10% growth.

clarifying_info.q: What is ABC's current market share by segment?

framework: Product: attributes, ease of use, value proposition, price — benchmark against competition
Customer: target market segment(s), brand loyalty, price sensitivity, important attributes, typical customer behavior (likes/dislikes), buying habits
Market: market share and trends, buying habits by segment
Distribution channel: distribution network coverage, shelf space and positioning relative to competitors, share of distribution network vs. competitors

questions.prompt: Question 2: One of ABC's biggest market segments is 18-55 year old women, but their share has been declining recently. Why might this be happening and how would you approach this issue?
questions.guidance: Suggest breaking the issue into: brand awareness, trial rate, re-trial/acceptance rate, and distribution access. Benchmark against Bell. Note that the women's segment is maturing (only 5% growth) while men's is growing faster (20%).

questions.prompt: Question 3: Using the segment data below, what sales are required for ABC to have 50% of the women's market in 2 years? (Women: $800M, 5% growth; Men: $200M, 20% growth; Teens: $100M, 10% growth)
questions.guidance: Calculate total women's market in 2 years, then take 50% of that.

math.setup: Total Women's Market in 2 years = 800 * (1.05)^2; Target = 50% of that total
math.answer: ABC needs $441M in women's segment sales to hold 50% share in 2 years.

questions.prompt: Question 4: What is ABC's current dollar market share? What will it be in 2 years if they maintain current share percentages? (Current shares: Women 50%, Men 10%, Teens 30%)
questions.guidance: Calculate current dollar market share by applying percentages to segment sizes, then project forward using growth rates. Note ABC's very low penetration in men's segment (10%) despite that segment's high 20% growth — a key insight to highlight.

math.setup: Current $ share = (share%) * (segment size) for each segment summed. Future $ share = same percentages applied to grown segment sizes.
math.answer: Current ABC dollar market share: $450M. In 2 years (maintaining same share %): $506.1M, representing 39.2% of total market (down from ~40.9% today, because faster-growing men's segment has low ABC penetration).

questions.prompt: Question 5: ABC conducted two surveys benchmarking against Bell in the 18-55 women segment. Survey 1 (Brand Awareness): Bell users — 80% know about ABC; Non-users — 40% know about ABC, 60% know about Bell; ABC users — 95% know about Bell. Survey 2 (Perception of Quality): ABC users — 95% say ABC is higher quality, 85% say Bell is higher quality; Bell users — 70% say ABC is higher quality, 95% say Bell is higher quality; Non-users — 55% say ABC is higher quality, 85% say Bell is higher quality. What do you notice and what should ABC do?
questions.guidance: Key observations: Despite ABC's high quality, Bell has superior brand awareness among non-users (60% vs 40%) and superior quality perception in all non-ABC-user groups. Even 85% of Bell users think Bell is higher quality vs 70% who think ABC is higher quality. Among non-users, more perceive Bell as higher quality (85%) than ABC (55%). ABC should focus on: (1) improving brand awareness via advertising, especially targeting non-users; (2) improving quality perception via promotions, joint retailer marketing, and trials/sampling programs.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key areas ABC should investigate to understand and address its declining revenues and market share?

categories.name: Product
ideas: Product attributes vs. competition (ease of use, color range, lasting power)
Value proposition and pricing relative to Bell

categories.name: Customer
ideas: What women value most in hair color (ease of use, quality, price)
Reasons for switching from ABC to Bell

categories.name: Market & Competition
ideas: Bell's recent moves (new products, pricing changes, promotions)
Segment growth trends — women maturing, men growing fast
Opportunity in underserved men's and teens segments

categories.name: Brand & Marketing
ideas: Advertising spend and effectiveness vs. Bell
Joint marketing with key retail partners

recommendation: The primary driver of ABC's declining revenues and market share is Bell's superior brand awareness and quality perception, especially among non-users. ABC must invest in advertising to close the awareness gap and in promotions, sampling, and joint retailer marketing to improve quality perception.
ABC has very low penetration in the fast-growing men's segment (10% share, 20% growth). This is the most immediate growth opportunity and should be prioritized for future targeting.
The teens segment is small ($100M) but growing at 10%. ABC should explore innovative products and increased marketing to expand total market size and capture share here.
risks: Advertising spend may not quickly shift entrenched Bell brand perceptions
Men's segment may require a distinct product line or branding strategy that ABC is not currently set up to deliver
Teens segment market expansion is uncertain and may require significant investment in new product development
next_steps: Conduct deeper consumer research on reasons for switching to Bell and barriers to trying ABC
Develop targeted advertising campaign to close brand awareness gap with Bell among non-users
Pilot joint marketing and in-store promotion programs with top retailers
Develop a go-to-market plan specifically for the men's hair color segment
Assess whether current ABC product line meets men's and teens' needs or if new SKUs are required
